what: full-table completion: the five remaining compared-table columns (RefCOCO testA/testB, RefCOCO+ testA/testB, RefCOCOg test(u)) evaluated with the same frozen components and the aligned protocol
protocol: mIoU = mean per-expression IoU; oIoU = pooled intersection/union, both from the per-expression records under the aligned protocol of protocol_audit.json; sentence-prompt box prior (the shipped rule)
published_source: GLOD-RIS Table I, test columns (same source as the audited val columns in protocol_audit.json)
pareto_ledger: Scoped precisely: the shipped method strictly exceeds the published GLOD-RIS row on 5 of 5 test-column mIoU values, on the three val mIoU and three val oIoU values (aligned re-evaluations, protocol_audit.json). Published test-column oIoU is not transcribed here (the paper's table shows published mIoU only), so no oIoU dominance claim is made on the test columns. GLOD-RIS does not report gRefCOCO, so our gRefCOCO results are compared there against the same-class floors (PSALM 42.0/43.3, SELF1E 44.4 cIoU) and the run's own prior record, per the 2026-10-08 operator standard -- not against GLOD-RIS. Beyond the mIoU/oIoU table, the ledger carries: reproducibility (their published numbers do not reproduce on our independent implementation: -25.7/-23.1/-20.6 mIoU vs the val columns, glodris_repro.json, ruled also causally by the same-pool rule swap) and API-independence (our path is fully local; GLOD-RIS's inference depends on a network MLLM API). One axis is not dominated and stays declared: the gRefCOCO path adds a second frozen detector next to the VLM prior.
